fi-cirrhilabrus-cyanogularis.title: Blue Throat Fairy Wrasse
fi-cirrhilabrus-cyanogularis.summary: A colorful, peaceful fairy wrasse from Indonesia and the Philippines. Males show more intense color during display.
rows: About 4 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 6.2 cm (2.4 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Carnivore. Frozen mysis, enriched brine shrimp and small meaty foods
Indo-West Pacific: Indonesia and the Philippines and photographed from Malaysia

fi-pseudocheilinus-hexataenia.title: Six Line Wrasse
fi-pseudocheilinus-hexataenia.summary: A small orange wrasse with six blue stripes. Hunts pests on live rock but can be pushy.
rows: About 3 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 10 cm (3.9 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Small crustaceans and other live-rock pests, plus frozen meaty foods
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea south to Natal, South Africa and east to the Tuamoto Islands, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to Lord Howe and the Austral islands
notes: Known to eat pests such as pyramidellid snails and flatworms.
warn: May bully peaceful wrasses and other timid fish.

fi-cirrhilabrus-ryukyuensis.title: Yellow-Flanked Fairy Wrasse
fi-cirrhilabrus-ryukyuensis.summary: A fairy wrasse with a greenish-blue head and a yellow triangle on the side. Peaceful and active in reef tanks.
rows: Carnivore. Vitamin-enriched frozen mysis and brine shrimp
Western Pacific: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines; north to Taiwan and the Ryukyu Islands, Japan
notes: A jumper; use a tight lid.

fi-paracheilinus-carpenteri.title: Carpenter's Flasher Wrasse
fi-paracheilinus-carpenteri.summary: A small, peaceful flasher wrasse. Males put on bright fin displays, especially with females present.
rows: Can be kept in groups; females encourage the male to display
Carnivore. Vitamin-enriched frozen mysis and brine shrimp, other meaty foods, marine flake and pellets
Western Pacific: Philippines, north to Taiwan and Iriomotejima, south to northern Bali and Flores

fi-wetmorella-albofasciata.title: White Banded Possum Wrasse
fi-wetmorella-albofasciata.summary: One of the smallest wrasses in the hobby, red-brown to yellow with two white bars and eye-spots on its fins. A secretive fish that hovers in shaded caves.
rows: About 3 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 6 cm (2.4 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Foods: copepods, brine shrimp, mysis shrimp, live small invertebrates, finely chopped frozen carnivore foods
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Hawaiian and Society islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef; Pohnpei and Marshall Islands in Micronesia
notes: Keep with small, mild fish such as gobies; boisterous tangs and big damsels push it off its food.
